plan.why: A contrarian-but-true correction of an overstated headline in the search-question format of our #2 Short ('Does Mounjaro speed up metabolism?'). It's a different angle from the 09-28 muscle carousel. | fact-check: The source is real: Brancato D et al., 'Real-world effectiveness of 6-month tirzepatide therapy on body weight and composition in adults with overweight and obesity', J Diabetes Complications 2026;40(11):109419, doi:10.1016/j.jdiacomp.2026.109419. Details: retrospective, no control arm, n=122, two centres in Palermo, Italy, 79.5% female, people with type 2 diabetes and prior GLP-1 users excluded, treatment completers only, body composition by bioelectrical impedance (BIA). Fat mass −35.4%, fat-free mass −5.1%, skeletal muscle mass 'remained stable'. Framing problem: the angle calls it a 'myth-bust of tirzepatide preserves muscle', but this paper itself reports stable skeletal muscle. Calling it a myth would contradict the source. Being a small, completers-only BIA study doesn't make it false, so it's 'not proven', not 'a myth'. The honest angle is 'what this study can and can't tell you'. Key limits to state: BIA estimates muscle and is sensitive to hydration, completers only, no control group, mostly women, no people with T2D. Also note that a separate small US real-world BIA study (Frontiers in Endocrinology 2026, n=35, about 81 weeks) reported skeletal muscle mass down 8.3%, so findings vary. Anchor to the SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy (adults with BMI 30+, or 27+ with a weight-related condition, without diabetes): about three-quarters of the weight lost was fat and about a quarter was lean mass. Copy the exact figures from the paper. Tirzepatide is the generic name, and Zepbound/Mounjaro are for recognition only.

package.title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): Fat Loss or Muscle Loss? #shorts
package.description:
On tirzepatide, is the weight you lose fat or muscle? A 24-week real-world Italian study of 122 adults with overweight or obesity (no type 2 diabetes) found fat mass down 35.4% on average and fat-free mass down 5.1%, with muscle estimated stable by bioimpedance. But it used past records, had no control group, counted finishers only and was mostly women. A randomized SURMOUNT-1 substudy (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes; 124 tirzepatide vs 36 placebo, 72 weeks) found about three-quarters of weight lost was fat and a quarter lean mass (not only muscle), in both groups. Common side effects are mostly tummy-related, like nausea, and usually ease over time.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. It's a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
Real-world tirzepatide body composition study — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jdiacomp.2026.109419
SURMOUNT-1 body composition substudy — https://europepmc.org/articles/pmc11965027
SURMOUNT-1 (NEJM) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2206038

social.instagram_caption:
Fat or muscle — what actually comes off on tirzepatide? 🧬

A 24-week real-world study of 122 adults with overweight or obesity (no type 2 diabetes) tracked body composition on tirzepatide (Mounjaro):
- Fat mass: down 35.4% on average
- Fat-free mass: down 5.1%
- Estimated muscle: stable

The catch: this was retrospective, no control group, finishers only, mostly women, and muscle was estimated with bioimpedance (hydration can skew it).

For a cleaner comparison, a randomized SURMOUNT-1 substudy scanned 160 adults without diabetes with obesity (or overweight plus a weight-related condition): 124 on tirzepatide, 36 on placebo. Over 72 weeks: weight fell 21.3% vs 5.3%. In follow-up analysis, about three-quarters of the weight lost was fat and a quarter was lean mass (not only muscle) — in both groups, not just tirzepatide.

What experts suggest to help protect lean mass: protein at every meal (unless your clinician has told you to limit protein, e.g. kidney disease) and strength training. Common side effects are mostly digestive — like nausea — and usually ease over time.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate and safe. It passes, with 5 small wording fixes listed below.

**Italian study (Brancato 2026), checked against the DOI record and a news write-up:** I couldn't open the full text (403 from Elsevier), so I couldn't confirm the numbers in the paper itself. The script matches what I could see:
- a retrospective study at two centres in Palermo, Italy
- 122 people who finished 24 weeks, 79.5% women, no type 2 diabetes
- muscle and fat measured by bioimpedance (BIA)
- fat mass down 35.4%, fat-free mass down 5.1%, skeletal muscle mass stable
- the limits the script names are the ones the authors list: retrospective, no control group, finishers only, mostly women, one region

**SURMOUNT-1 substudy (Look 2025), checked against the published record:**
- 160 people had DXA scans: 124 on tirzepatide, 36 on placebo
- at 72 weeks, about 75% of weight lost was fat and 25% was lean mass, in both groups
- the 75/25 split comes from a post hoc analysis, done after the trial
- the published correction only fixes an axis label on one figure, so it doesn't affect the script

**Framing and safety:** the script keeps "estimated" muscle, explains that fat-free mass isn't the same as muscle, and is honest about the limits. The protein advice carries the kidney caveat, the prescriber line is word for word, and there's no dosing.

**The 5 fixes:**
- Add how many people were in each SURMOUNT-1 group, plus the absolute numbers.
- Say the 75/25 split is post hoc.
- Add a short side-effect line, as the niche rules ask.
- Soften "burn" in the opening narration.
- Cite a source for the protein and strength-training advice, or attribute it to expert guidance.

issues.claim: Over 72 weeks, about three-quarters of weight lost was fat, a quarter lean mass. Similar on tirzepatide and placebo; tirzepatide users just lost more.
issues.problem: The size of each group is missing: the placebo group had only 36 people, versus 124 on tirzepatide. The absolute changes are also missing (craft rule: every number needs its comparator). And the 75/25 split comes from a post hoc analysis, which the script doesn't say.
issues.fix: Narration: "A randomized SURMOUNT-1 substudy scanned 160 adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes: 124 on tirzepatide, 36 on placebo. Over 72 weeks, weight fell 21.3% vs 5.3%. In a later analysis, about three-quarters of weight lost was fat and a quarter lean mass, in both groups. Tirzepatide users just lost more." Add to the items list: "124 tirzepatide · 36 placebo · post hoc split".

issues.claim: Does Mounjaro's tirzepatide burn fat or muscle?
issues.problem: "Mounjaro's tirzepatide" reads awkwardly. "Burn" hints at a mechanism, but the studies only measured body composition. The title is acceptable as a search-style question.
issues.fix: Narration: "On tirzepatide, Mounjaro, do you lose fat or muscle?" On-screen text: "Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): fat or muscle?"

issues.problem: This is accurate. But DXA "lean mass" in s5 also isn't pure muscle, and viewers may read "lean" as muscle.
issues.fix: In s5, add after "a quarter lean mass": "(lean mass isn't only muscle)".

issues.problem: This scene has no source (source_ids is empty). Neither study tested protein or strength training.
issues.fix: Start the line with "Experts suggest" ("Experts suggest protein at every meal, unless your clinician has told you to limit protein, for example kidney disease, plus strength training."), and cite the medical-society guidance on nutrition with GLP-1 medicines in source_ids.
